Lessons.Title: Logarithmic Properties
ExplanationParagraphs: For any valid common base b, log_b(MN)=log_b M+log_b N, log_b(M/N)=log_b M−log_b N and log_b(M^k)=k log_b M, with all original log arguments positive.
Expand products and quotients after identifying positive variable restrictions; when condensation creates an expression, preserve original domains.
Use roots as rational exponents. For positive x, log_b(nth_root(x))=(1/n)log_b(x).
Any base b>0,b!=1 can be converted: log_b(x)=ln(x)/ln(b), for x>0.
For logarithmic equations, combine logs first, solve, then check all original argument domains and reject extraneous roots.
An original source photograph illustrating a chemistry pH measurement is replaced by independent log-scale numerical examples; no publisher photo is copied.
Independent Cool-down: expand log((6x²)/y), condense 2lnx−lnz and solve log_2(x+1)=3.
Independent Try It 8: Expand ln((x² y)/sqrt z).
Independent Try It 13: Express log_11 7 using ln.
Independent Try It 14: Evaluate log_2 13 to 5 decimals.

KeyConcepts.Title: Product rule
KeyConcepts.Rule: Sum of logs represents a positive product.

KeyConcepts.Title: Change of base
KeyConcepts.Rule: Numerical calculators support common and natural logarithms.

Visuals.Description: Original educational numerical replacement for chemistry photograph; sample H+ concentration relates to pH=−log10[H+]. No original image copied.

SummaryPoints: Use product, quotient and power rules.
Preserve original domains when combining logs.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Sum inside a logarithm is not a product.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Ignore individual argument positivity when condensing.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The condensed result may define extra input values.
